message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different kinds of workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – originally for drawing pixels on screen, now also used for massively parallel compute tasks. |
| **Core count** | Few cores (typically 2–32 in consumer CPUs). | Hundreds or thousands of smaller cores (e.g., 1,000+ CUDA cores in modern GPUs). |
| **Execution style** | Serial/low‑parallelism – each core can handle complex branching and control flow. | SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) – many cores execute the same instruction on different data simultaneously. |
| **Clock speed** | Higher clock speeds (≈3–5 GHz) because fewer cores and more complex logic per core. | Lower clock speeds (≈1–1.5 GHz) because many cores share resources and focus on throughput. |
| **Cache & memory hierarchy** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches per core; tightly coupled with system RAM via high‑bandwidth bus. | Smaller per‑core cache; relies on high‑bandwidth VRAM (GDDR6/7) and dedicated memory bus. |
| **Instruction set** | Complex, rich instruction sets (x86, ARM) with support for branches, exceptions, etc. | Simplified, highly parallel instruction set (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan/SPIR-V) optimized for vector operations. |
| **Typical workloads** | Single‑threaded or lightly threaded tasks, OS kernel, database queries, web servers. | Highly parallel tasks: rendering frames, physics simulations, machine learning inference/training, scientific computations. |
| **Energy efficiency** | Optimized for low latency per operation; power scales with number of active cores. | Optimized for throughput; power scales with number of active threads but each core consumes less power individually. |

### Why the difference matters

* **Latency vs Throughput** – CPUs excel at low‑latency, sequential work; GPUs excel at high‑throughput, data‑parallel work.
* **Programming models** – CPUs use traditional multi‑threading (OpenMP, pthreads); GPUs use data‑parallel frameworks (CUDA, OpenCL, DirectX12, Vulkan).
* **Cost & form factor** – CPUs are integrated into motherboards; GPUs are discrete cards (though integrated GPUs exist in many CPUs).

In practice, most modern systems combine both: the CPU handles general tasks while the GPU accelerates graphics and compute‑heavy workloads.
